technical-summary: Session record schema restructured v2 (flat) -> v3 (grouped, omit-if-absent): provider-id/model-id/metadata under 'provider', all four timestamps under 'timing', idle/max-lifetime under 'policy' (whole group omitted when unset), turn-count/request-ids under 'activity'; close-reason/error stay top-level but only when actually set. v2->v3 migration added alongside the existing v1->v2 step (both run transparently on read). Added sessions_store.py accessor helpers (session_provider_id, session_model_id, session_turn_count, etc.) and updated every read call site across sessions.py/dispatch.py/api.py; transition_session_record and record_session_turn now write into the grouped locations directly (no shim). Found and fixed a real bug this surfaced: list_execution_sessions sorted by the now-nonexistent top-level r['created-at'], which would have crashed session listing entirely. Also fixed gpt-auto's GptAutoSessionTransport ignoring its own GptAutoConfig.cdp_url in favor of an always-unset duplicate constructor parameter with a hardcoded default -- any configured custom CDP port was silently ignored. Along the way, discovered and fixed a second real, independent gpt-auto resume bug: _resolve_workspace's resume branches called client.evaluate('window.location.href=...') assuming an active browser page already existed, which is false right after a fresh CdpClient connection ('No active page'); replaced with client.new_tab(url), which both guarantees a page and navigates in one step -- verified this closed the failure by driving a real close->resume->recall round trip against a live ChatGPT session via CDP. Registered three production error codes that were raised but never added to error-resolutions.yaml (VAL-AGW-102, VAL-AGW-103, RES-AGW-103), which is itself an architecture-doctrine violation this work surfaced -- any code path hitting them previously crashed with a generic ValueError instead of the intended typed error. Updated ~10 test call sites for the new schema shape and fixed unrelated pre-existing test gaps the investigation surfaced (missing surface_id in several session-binding test fixtures; one test asserting since-removed pre-hardening v1-migration behavior, rewritten to assert the current fail-closed contract). Verified: full unit session test sweep (100% pass), plus two directly relevant Docker E2E suites on real Linux against the real pi-acp bridge -- pi-acp-resume-e2e (drives AcpAgentSessionTransport.open_resumed() through a genuine SIGKILL-and-resume) and pi-rpc-tap-e2e (real multi-turn tool-calling conversation) -- both pass (one transient tool-calling flake on first run, passed clean on retry, consistent with that test's own documented small-model uncertainty).
user-summary-candidate: Restructured how gateway sessions are stored internally (cleaner, grouped shape instead of one flat list of fields) and fixed several bugs it surfaced along the way, including a session-listing crash and a gpt-auto resume bug.

technical-summary: dispatch_request now routes a no-isolation provider's plain one-shot submit (no session_id/session_keep_alive) through the existing ephemeral-session pattern in _dispatch_session_request (open, one turn, auto-close) instead of the disposable-subprocess worker path, which categorically requires full-isolation. full-isolation and partial-isolation routing, worker_host.py's UNS-AGW-076 gate, and SH06's Docker-validated subprocess isolation model are unchanged. UNS-AGW-076's resolution text rewritten to state it no longer applies to no-isolation providers and to point at session_keep_alive as the working alternative. Added a unit test proving the new routing never touches execute_isolated_provider_turn for a no-isolation provider.
user-summary-candidate: agent_task_submit now works for browser/CDP-driven and other no-isolation providers (e.g. gpt-auto) even without opening a live session explicitly -- previously every plain one-shot submit for these providers failed immediately with UNS-AGW-076.

A new providers_api.get_provider_load_errors() accessor exposes residual failures, surfaced through gateway_overview()'s new diagnostics block (providers_loaded, skipped_count, errors) and forwarded unchanged by the agent_task_gateway_overview MCP tool. "line-length" suppression for provider YAML descriptors is a yamllint per-rule ignore glob, not a yaml-language-server setting (verified against the installed yaml-language-server package's settingsHandlers.js -- no such key exists there). (2) .vscode/settings.json's yaml.* keys (validate/completion/schemas/customTags -- the genuinely VS-Code-only part), written through a new providers/surfaces/host_settings.py that reuses extensions_json.py's host-adapter-routed isolation pattern; HostAdapter gained a settings_manifest field (hosts.yaml: vscode.settings-manifest) instead of hardcoding the path. technical-summary: Extended CC58's lint-config projection with TypeScript support (follow-up to the initial Python/YAML implementation). typescript.yaml's compilerOptions projects to tsconfig.json (merged into any existing file so hand-authored include/exclude/references survive re-projection, matching the same merge discipline used for .vscode/settings.json). format.semi/singleQuote/trailingComma project to .prettierrc.json using prettier's real documented option names. format.tabSize/insertSpaces project to a [*.{ts,tsx}] section in .editorconfig via a new section-preserving merge helper, rather than duplicating them into .prettierrc.json's non-standard tabWidth/useTabs or into VS Code settings -- .editorconfig is a genuine cross-editor standard (VS Code, IntelliJ, vim, emacs all read it natively), so all three TypeScript outputs stay in the native-tool-config bucket with no VS Code-only glue required.

technical-summary: Chromium gates remote debugging on the default browser profile behind user consent: the DevTools HTTP discovery endpoints (/json/version, /json/list) return 404 while the CDP websocket remains functional. puppeteer.connect({browserURL}) must GET /json/version to learn the websocket URL, so gpt-auto's connect failed before reaching a working transport. A dedicated --user-data-dir is not an option because gpt-auto requires the default profile, where the logged-in ChatGPT session and workspace live. Fix: the Node helper (gpt_auto_cdp.cjs) now attempts browserURL and falls back to browserWSEndpoint only when that connect actually fails, so the connect itself is the probe and no check-then-use race exists. cdp_client.py resolves the fallback endpoint from the browser's DevToolsActivePort file, restricted to a single user-data directory (AUDIAGENTIC_GPT_AUTO_USER_DATA_DIR, else the supported browser default) and to loopback cdp_url hosts, validating the port range and the /devtools/browser/ path prefix; enumerating multiple Chromium-family installs could only contribute a websocket UUID belonging to a different browser instance, and a local file cannot describe a remote browser. The whole connect RPC is bounded by a 15s timeout that kills the Node helper on expiry, because puppeteer sets no websocket handshake timeout and a stale endpoint hangs indefinitely; bounding it inside Node with Promise.race would leave the losing connect() able to open a socket nobody owns. IPv6 loopback hosts are bracketed when building the websocket authority. Verified against a live browser: tests/gpt_auto/test_cdp_event_wiring.py 6/6, plus a full agents-gateway request and a two-turn keep-alive session.
user-summary-candidate: The gpt-auto ChatGPT browser provider works again after a Chromium change began refusing DevTools HTTP discovery on the default browser profile.

technical-summary: Consolidated duplicated provider automation-mode vocabulary and validation across the providers component: added contracts/automation_vocabulary.py with three shared narrow Literal aliases (ProviderAutomationMode/ProviderReconcileMode/ProviderApplyStatusMode) and re-pointed 7 family Mode aliases at them; switched 4 family handlers (managed-mcp, language-server-projection, model-projection, plugin-entry) from hardcoded mode frozensets to catalogue-backed family.supported_modes validation; derived lifecycle_modes.py's CLI mode set from CliLifecycleMode instead of a stale hand-copy, which restores MCP-level reachability of the already-implemented upgrade/upgrade-status CLI lifecycle modes; added ObserverInstallationTiming and SelfProvidedLspResult.state validation where none existed; fixed a reason-string typo in managed-MCP status; deleted two confirmed-stale duplicate schema files; consolidated ProviderIsolationTier's three independent definitions down to one shared source for providers_api/descriptors.base, with agents/contracts/execution_context.py kept as a documented, TYPE_CHECKING-only exception because it sits on the gateway worker subprocess's top-level import path, where a runtime providers-package import would corrupt the worker's stdout-framed IPC protocol (discovered via test failure, not assumed).
user-summary-candidate: Cleaned up duplicated provider mode/type definitions across the codebase and fixed a bug where the CLI's upgrade/upgrade-status actions were unreachable through the agent tools despite being fully implemented.

technical-summary: The post-commit ledger-stamp hook has never recorded a commit SHA: 0 of 225 ledger events carry git-commits. Two independent causes. (1) git_commits.py, which the hook invokes, was deleted by 3e0b67697 (2026-07-18) as unreachable dead code -- correct by importer scan, since its only caller is a shell hook where the import sits inside a quoted string. The hook then failed with ModuleNotFoundError on every commit, swallowed by 2>/dev/null || true. (2) Structurally, the hook stamped fragments in .audiagentic/runtime/ledger/fragments/, but record_change_event calls record_change(sync=True), which syncs and purges the fragment inside the same synchronous call; recording is not async, so the window in which a fragment exists at commit time is deterministically zero. Restored git_commits.py at components/source_control/ and retargeted it to stamp unreleased entries in CURRENT_RELEASE_LEDGER.ndjson, where events actually live; the historical ledger is never rewritten because released events must not be restamped. Measured cost: 0.2ms parse/scan/serialize against a ~200ms hook dominated by interpreter start and two git subprocesses. Carried CC42's pending migration by using foundation.io atomic writes rather than reintroducing the non-atomic write that item flagged. Fixed install_post_commit_hook, which returned installed=True on a legacy marker without rewriting the body, permanently freezing any pre-managed-block hook at its original entry point; it now upgrades the legacy body to a managed block, falling back to appending when the legacy region cannot be delimited. Hook errors are no longer suppressed -- git ignores a post-commit exit code, so a broken hook cannot fail a commit, but a silent one hides its own breakage. Replaced the test assertion that string-matched the entry-point name in the hook body with one deriving that name from a real import, so deletion of the symbol now fails the test instead of passing.
user-summary-candidate: Change-log entries are now linked to the commits that implemented them; the hook responsible had been silently doing nothing.

technical-summary: Unified the MCP tool error path across all 15 registered servers (143 tools). Renamed the log_tool_call decorator to tool_boundary and folded in exception redaction/translation: tools now raise ToolError with redacted, code+resolution-bearing text instead of either propagating raw (unredacted) exceptions or returning an {ok: False} error dict disguised as a successful result. Deleted report_error() and unwound its 25 call sites in project_mcp.py/session_mcp.py, including 3 return-type unions that existed only to carry the error dict. Closed a real redaction gap: AudiaGenticError.__str__ never redacted its own message text, so secret-shaped content in a domain error's message reached callers unredacted even through the old report_error() path. Adjacent fix: build_sectioned_body() in foundation/workflow/frontmatter.py rendered an empty heading for any blank custom plan-doc section with no way to remove it; now a blank custom section is dropped on render (canonical sections still always render).
user-summary-candidate: MCP tool calls now report errors consistently and safely: failures raise a proper tool error with a redacted, actionable message instead of sometimes leaking raw exception text or silently returning a fake-successful result.

Incorporated four into their parent items: AS87 gained a typed page/source-state contract (truncation/retention gap, corrupt/missing indexed events) on its cursor read so AS94 can consume it without inspecting relay files directly; AS93's step 4 now sources events from SessionEvidenceProjection.accept()'s correlated evidence instead of the context-free SessionLifecycleDecision, and its exclusion wording now states project-isolation directly instead of a stale caller-authorization deferral; AS94's cursor step now owns only outer syntax/context binding, delegating generation/retention-gap semantics to AS93 and AS87 respectively, dropped the phantom 'task id' identity, and fixed stale 'authorized caller' wording; AS95's control-idempotency rule now explicitly handles the same-control-id-different-context collision case. RV928 was already incorporated into AS92's notes (closed as-is). RV896 was closed with a rationale note: its findings were resolved by AS63's Phase 2 work and validated by AS81's closure, both of which landed after the review was written.
